en.title: Defamation in Bangladesh Explained Simply
en.directAnswer: Defamation law deals with statements that harm reputation, but the Penal Code also contains important exceptions. Truth, public good, good-faith opinions and protected communications can matter. Do not assume that every criticism, bad review or false statement is automatically criminal defamation.

atAGlance.whoFor: A citizen wants to know when a reputation-harming statement may be defamation.
atAGlance.legalBasis: Penal Code, 1860, defamation provisions and exceptions; other civil law as applicable.
atAGlance.mainRule: The exact words, audience, truth, purpose and good faith matter.
atAGlance.updateStatus: Very high-risk. Final version should cite the exact Penal Code sections and exceptions after lawyer review.

en.lawMeaning: The exact words, audience, truth, purpose and good faith matter. This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Save where and when they were published.
Preserve evidence of falsity or context.
Consider whether a statutory exception may apply.
Get legal advice before filing or sending a legal notice.
evidence: Post/link; screenshot; video; publication date; witnesses; evidence of actual facts; loss/damage records.
en.simpleExample: A customer writes a negative but honest review. The business should not assume “negative = defamation.” The exact statement and legal exceptions need review.
commonMistakes: Common mistakes: Threatening arrest over criticism.
Common mistakes: filing before checking exceptions.
